subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram `sessions_spawn(thread:true, mode:"session")` create and bind a child forum topic for explicit subagent sessions, or should Telegram keep current-conversation binding as the supported behavior unless a narrower opt-in is designed?
rationale: Current main already supports Telegram current-conversation binding through the core adapter path, but the remaining requested child-topic behavior changes user-visible routing and conflicts with the open request to avoid user-visible internal sub-agent threads.

options.title: Sponsor narrowed child-topic support
options.body: Repair or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 so explicit subagent thread spawns can create child forum topics while normal Telegram placement stays current.

options.title: Keep current-conversation only
options.body: Close or narrow this feature after documenting that Telegram binds subagent sessions to the current topic/conversation and does not create child topics by default.

options.title: Defer to channel policy design
options.body: Hold this request behind the broader channel threading policy so Telegram routing semantics follow the accepted cross-channel capability model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor narrowed child-topic support
recommendation.body: Repair or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 so explicit subagent thread spawns can create child forum topics while normal Telegram placement stays current.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision extends the core SessionBindingService direction introduced in the merged core thread-binding refactor.
